sections.label: Combined borrowing limit under GSA
sections.summary: Merging the Acts combines the LTBA and GSA borrowing limits of $105 billion and $960 billion into a single $1,065 billion limit under the renamed GSA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: With the merger of the Acts, the current borrowing limits under the LTBA and GSA, which are $105 billion and $960 billion respectively, will be combined to form a single borrowing limit of $1,065 billion under the renamed GSA.

sections.label: Repeal of borrowing Acts
sections.summary: The Bill repeals the External Loans Act, Treasury Deposit Receipts Act and borrowing provisions in the Developmental Investment Fund Act.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Specifically, the Bill will repeal the External Loans Act and Treasury Deposit Receipts Act, as well as borrowing provisions in the Developmental Investment Fund Act.

sections.label: Renamed GSA and SINGA borrowing
sections.summary: The Government will use the renamed GSA for non-spending borrowing and SINGA for infrastructure spending, with SGS bonds renamed to reflect these purposes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Going forward, the Government will rely on the renamed GSA to borrow for specific non-spending purposes and the SINGA to borrow for spending on nationally significant infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For example, the new SGS issued for infrastructure financing has been named as SGS(Infrastructure) bonds and the existing SGS bonds renamed as SGS(Market Development) bonds to reflect the different purposes of borrowing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Borrowings for non-spending purposes, which will be consolidated under the renamed GSA in this Bill, will continue to make up the majority of Singapore Government's borrowings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Through this Bill, we will provide greater clarity on the Government's debt profile.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Earlier this year, the House has also passed the Significant Infrastructure Government Loan Act (SINGA) in which the proceeds raised can only be used to fund major and very long-term key infrastructures.

sections.label: SSGS share of SGS
sections.summary: The member states the main bulk of Government securities is SSGS, which he believes account for over 70% of the SGS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: My third question is, the main bulk of the securities issued by the Government is the Special Singapore Government Securities (SSGS) which I believe account for about over 70% of the SGS.

sections.label: Suggestion to reclassify SSGS
sections.summary: The member suggests MOF classify privately placed SSGS held by the CPF Board as CPF Bonds under a separate borrowing limit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: These CPF related issuances, the SSGS, are also not invested by external investors because it is hold by the CPF Board, and its size of issuance and coupon rates therefore do not have any impact on the Singapore bond market nor its liquidity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Hence, I would suggest that MOF consider classifying these private placed securities which it privately placed to CPF Board as CPF Bond rather than called it the SGS, and it should come under a separate borrowing limit and, of course, to be approved by Parliament and the President.

sections.label: Clause 14 borrowing limit
sections.summary: Clause 14 proposes a Government loans borrowing limit of $1.065 trillion, combining the $960 billion securities and $105 billion Treasury Bills limits.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The first point worth noting is that clause 14 with the Bill proposes to set the borrowing limit for Government loans at $1.065 trillion, which represents the combined limits of $960 billion for the Government securities and $105 billion Treasury Bills that currently exists under two separate Acts.

sections.label: Debt ceiling risks
sections.summary: Fiscal rules like a reasonable debt limit can ensure sustainability, but a too frequently binding debt ceiling can harm government operation, as in the United States.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While fiscal rules such as a reasonable debt limit have been used in many countries and can play an important role in ensuring the sustainability of fiscal affairs, a debt ceiling that is too frequently binding can wreak havoc on the efficient operation of government, as the experience of the United States, where bipartisan brinksmanship routinely plagues efforts to raise the debt ceiling, reminds us.

sections.label: Clause 20 restricts MAS deposits
sections.summary: Clause 20 of the Bill restricts other Government entities, particularly MAS, from accepting advance deposits in anticipation of raising loans via Treasury Bills.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The second point, Mr Speaker, I wish to raise has to do with how clause 20 of the Bill restricts the ability of other Government entities, in particular, MAS from accepting advance deposits in anticipation of raising loans by way of Treasury Bills.

sections.label: CBDCs and MAS flexibility
sections.summary: The speaker asks if the Bill precludes MAS from accepting advance deposits for Treasury Bills needed for CBDCs, but supports the Bill despite reservations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While the detailed findings of this exercise have yet to be made public, it is reasonable to ask if the practical implementation of CBDCs may yet require flexibility for MAS to be able to accept such advance deposits for Treasury Bills and if this Bill would preclude such action.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Hence, while I accept that these two conditions are somewhat unusual, it is nevertheless worth asking if this particular clause in the Bill may unnecessarily tie the hands of the MAS to operate in a modern global macroeconomic environment.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding these reservations and questions, Mr Speaker, I support the Bill.

sections.label: Single borrowing limit
sections.summary: New section 11 of the Act will replace separate borrowing limits for Government securities and Treasury Bills with a single borrowing limit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 11 of the Act will replace the separate borrowing limits for Government securities and Treasury Bills with a single borrowing limit.

sections.label: Approval for borrowing beyond limit
sections.summary: The second point concerns the approval required for borrowing beyond the $1.065 trillion limit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My second point is on the approval required for borrowing beyond the $1.065 trillion limit.

sections.label: $1.065 trillion limit
sections.summary: The $1.065 trillion limit appears to make no difference.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The $1.065 trillion limit appears to make no difference.

sections.label: LTBA and GSA amounts
sections.summary: As at 30 September, $65 billion is under the LTBA and $699 billion under the GSA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As at 30 September, we have $65 billion under the LTBA and $699 billion under the GSA.

sections.label: Distinguishing borrowing purposes
sections.summary: The Government wants to distinguish borrowing for non-spending under LTBA and GSA from borrowing for infrastructure under SINGA, which is spent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: He had suggested to pool it together as one combined limit, together with SINGA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But from the Government's point of view, for better governance and for better control of processes, we want to distinguish between borrowing for non-spending, which is done under LTBA and GSA, and borrowing under SINGA, which is borrowing for infrastructure, which we spend.

sections.label: GSA borrowing proceeds invested
sections.summary: Under the GSA, all of the borrowing proceeds are invested.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Under the GSA, all of the borrowing proceeds are invested.

sections.label: Borrowing limit as safeguard
sections.summary: The borrowing limit is not a permanent hard cap but serves as an additional layer of checks and safeguards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Our view is that this borrowing limit, while it is not a permanent hard cap, serve as an additional layer of checks and safeguards.
